paper_title: On the Role of Model Prior in Real-World Inductive Reasoning
caption: Human pairwise comparison results on three datasets, showing preferences for hypotheses with, without demos, and cases where it was hard to tell the difference.
model_annotation: This chart presents the results of human pairwise comparisons across three datasets – Truthful Review, Funny Reddit, and Unhealthy Comments – regarding preferences for hypotheses with or without demonstrations, or when it was difficult to determine a preference. Each dataset is represented by a separate pie chart, each containing four slices. For the Truthful Review chart, the slices are labeled “W/o Demos” (grey), “Hard to Tell” (blue), “W/ Demos” (light green), and an unlabeled section, with corresponding proportions of 43.0%, 22.9%, 34.1%, respectively; percentage labels are shown within each slice. The Funny Reddit chart has slices labeled “W/o Demos” (grey), “Hard to Tell” (blue), “W/ Demos” (light green), with proportions of 41.5%, 21.5%, and 37.1%, respectively, again with internal percentage labels. Finally, the Unhealthy Comments chart’s slices represent “W/o Demos” (grey), “Hard to Tell” (blue), “W/ Demos” (light green), with corresponding proportions of 34.8%, 27.4%, and 37.8%, and also include percentage labels within the slices. A legend is provided above the charts which associates colors with the categories “W/o Demos”, “Hard to Tell”, and “W/ Demos”. In each chart, the slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest proportion.
